source.title: From Generalization Analysis to Optimization Designs for State Space Models

record.tranche_reason: Reports experiments on SSMs that extend generalization analysis to sequence data and test new initialization and regularization methods; it does not test the claim versions' specified methods or properties.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own synthetic and LRA generalization results. Cited results from prior work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study develops a sequence-dependent SSM generalization bound and evaluates its own initialization and regularization methods. None of its results tests V1–V8. Its complexity measure is not magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness; its regularizer is not dropout. Using Adam/AdamW, fixed batches, or different model sizes without the required comparisons does not test the corresponding versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors derive a data-dependent bound for single-layer SSMs, use it to motivate initialization rescaling and a new regularizer, and report more robust synthetic output scales and improved test performance with modest computational overhead. LRA initialization benefits are weaker with normalization, regularizer gains depend on task and coefficient, and the theory does not cover the multilayer experimental models or feature dependencies.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes a data-dependent SSM complexity bound, initialization rescaling, and a new regularizer; it does not use the original versions' interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Synthetic outcomes vary with temporal-pattern coefficient b. LRA initialization effects are weaker with batch or layer normalization; regularization coefficient sensitivity is greater on Pathfinder and PathX.

fits_no_version.finding: Initialization rescaling lowers synthetic training loss and reduces its variation across temporal settings; baseline losses 0.15, 0.67, 2.50 become 0.11, 0.27, 0.20.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sequence-dependent initialization rescaling improves optimization robustness for the tested one-layer SSM.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed complexity measure and test loss covary across synthetic temporal settings. Table 1 reports the complexity values separately; these are not captured by the listed test-loss rows. This is not a sharpness measurement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A sequence-statistics complexity measure tracks test loss across the tested synthetic temporal settings.

fits_no_version.finding: The proposed regularizer lowers synthetic test loss at all three b values, while increasing training loss; combining it with rescaling gives the lowest reported synthetic test losses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed sequence-dependent regularizer improves held-out regression performance for the tested one-layer SSM.

fits_no_version.finding: With coefficient tuning, regularization raises mean LRA accuracy in 11 of 12 principal task-model comparisons; S4-Legs Retrieval decreases from 91.21 to 91.17. Several gains are small relative to reported standard errors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed regularizer can improve SSM sequence-classification accuracy, with effects depending on task, model, and regularization strength.

record.problems: The SSM theory is for single-layer linear models, while experiments include multilayer models; the high-dimensional method treats features as independent. The LRA baseline reproduction differs from the cited original due to software versions. Some regularization coefficients are selected using validation performance.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 9–13 and the additional ablations are omitted to stay within the 60-row limit; the primary synthetic results (Table 1) and principal LRA comparison (Table 2) are retained. The prose-reported sensitivity findings are summarized in method_sensitivity.

untested.parts: All: no fixed random-label fitting and natural-label generalization comparison.
All: no width sweep establishing interpolation and subsequent test-error behavior; small-model experiments change several training and architecture settings.
All: no convolutional-versus-fully-connected image-classifier comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
All: no adaptive-optimizer-versus-SGD comparison or optimizer-tuning study.
All: no controlled batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted recipes.
All: no dropout intervention; listed dropout settings are training configuration, not evidence of its effect.
All: no magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness, gap-ranking comparison, or controlled low-training-loss convolutional family.
All: no influence-based memorization estimates, example removal, or retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: All extracted numerical values and baselines match Tables 1–2. These rows describe the study's own methods and comparators, so they should not serve as evidence rows for V1–V8. No missing result bears on those versions; omitted appendices likewise do not test them. T3 requires a result on a claim version, not merely a new study of generalization.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the stated tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout effects and the stated training-set regimes.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.

relation.reason: It discusses generalization and regularization broadly, without testing the catalog's specific comparisons or relying on them as tools.

tranche.reason: The study evaluates its own SSM initialization and regularization methods and neither tests nor uses the specific findings in V1–V8.

source_check.notes: All sampled values match the tables; these own-method comparisons provide no evidence for V1–V8. Table 2 reports coefficient-tuned results with standard errors over three independent runs; the theory does not cover multilayer SSMs or feature dependencies.
